title: Family still seeks answer in police custody death
subtitle: It will be four years this May since Normand Jeanveau died while in the custody of Greater Sudbury Police and the family said they are still looking for answers.
article: It will be four years this May since Normand Jeanveau died while in the custody of Greater Sudbury Police and the family said they are still looking for answers.

On May 11 2007, a 9-1-1 call was made by Jeanveau's mother, Pauline Castonguay, asking for an ambulance to attend her Bellevue Street residences. Pauline Castonguy stated her son had fallen in the living room and needed medical attention. Jeanveau became aggressive and uncooperative after paramedics arrived and police were called in to assist.

Jeanveau was pepper-sprayed by police and continued to resist so he was handcuffed. Once handcuffed, he stopped struggling and went into medical distress. Paramedics began resuscitative efforts and transported Jeanveau to St. Joseph's Health Centre, where he was pronounced dead at 12:30 a.m.
Jeanveau's uncle, Larry Castonguay said Jeanveau's body had many bruises and cuts following the altercation.
"They said there was no excessive force used but no one could tell us what happened to his face or what happened to his body," he said. "Why were there bruises and cuts?"
Larry Castonguay said the family is organizing a rally to raise awareness on the case in an attempt to get closure.
"Now we want to get things rolling," he said. "That's why we have the t-shirts with the before and after pictures of my nephew, and we have some signs."
Larry Castonguay said the rally will be held in front of the Sudbury court house within a few weeks.

"We never got answers," he said. "We waited over a year for the (Special Investigations Unit) investigation and that led up to nothing. My lawyer seems to think this will go until the end of this year and I don't want it to go that long. We're tired of this, we're tired of dealing with it and we just want justice and answers."
